legend.mapchallenge.populationNote: Only cells with density ≥100 are drawn (2,773 cells, about 5.2 km² each). Population is the GHSL 2020 model estimate, not household registration.
legend.mapchallenge.facilityNote: Only cells with density ≥100 are drawn (about 5.2 km² each); each facility type has its own color ramp and fixed class breaks.
legend.mapchallenge.overlapNote: Hotspot = top 10% of populated cells in Taiwan (about 5.2 km² each). Overlap = share of population hotspots that are also facility hotspots.
legend.mapchallenge.tcchNote: Hotspot = top 10% within each county (about 0.74 km² fine cells); the two counties are not compared with each other.
legend.mapchallenge.source: GHSL GHS-POP R2023A 2020 (CC BY 4.0), MOEA factory registry 2026-06, MOI temple registry, MOE school directory, MOHW medical facilities, cram school directory, OpenStreetMap (ODbL, convenience stores); taipei-gis-analytics Day 4 cluster analysis
legend.mapchallenge.day05.method: Estimated from terrain + buildings + tree canopy; a view counts as continuous at ≥500 m with gaps ≤200 m; Green Island, Xiaoliuqiu, Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu not covered
legend.mapchallenge.day05.source: Terrain: MOI 20 m digital terrain model (2024); building height: GBA/OSM fusion; canopy height: Meta/WRI (CC BY 4.0); routes: OpenStreetMap (ODbL)
legend.mapchallenge.day05.seaViewNote: Rail is drawn thicker than roads; only routes within 3 km of the sea are shown. Trees within 40 m of the road are counted from 10 m canopy data (Meta/WRI); seawalls and coastal windbreak forests use assumed heights; the sea is taken at high tide (tidal flats count as sea); "through trees" means the view is partly blocked.
legend.mapchallenge.day06.license: Historical layers cited from: 中央研究院，《臺灣歷史文化地圖系統》第一版，（台北，中央研究院，2003年9月） (Academia Sinica, Taiwan History and Culture in Atlas, 1st ed., Sept 2003); licensed CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 Taiwan. This layer is derived data (TWD67 → WGS84, compared with present-day data) under the same terms; non-commercial.
legend.mapchallenge.day06.source: Present-day data: OpenStreetMap coastline (ODbL, retrieved 2026-11-06); MOI place names (2026-10-12) and village boundaries (2026-06-26); MOI national religion registry temples (retrieved 2026-08-01); Pulse lighthouse layer and CWA station list (update date not checked)
legend.mapchallenge.day06.places: Today's place names with 鯤鯓 / 塭 / 汕 (sandbar, fish pond, shoal); colour = latest era in which the spot was still west of the coastline
legend.mapchallenge.day06.coastNote: The three eras use three distinct hues; the oldest (17th–18th c.) line is drawn thicker. All three trace water/land boundaries including lagoons such as the Taijiang Inner Sea; the 19th-century line reaches as far inland as the 17th–18th century one around 23.05–23.15°N (original notes not checked).
legend.mapchallenge.day06.coastToday: Within the range shared by all three eras, median distance from the furthest inland water to today's outer coast: about 17.9 km (17th–18th c.), 7.6 km (19th c.), 2.0 km (early 20th c.).
legend.mapchallenge.day06.surviveYes: Name survives in today's village names ({n})
legend.mapchallenge.day06.taipeiNote: 74 towns (machi) and ōaza; a name counts as surviving when its stem appears in an overlapping present-day village name (e.g. Nishimon → Ximen Village). Names shown from z12; datum error about 50 m.
legend.mapchallenge.day06.templeTitle: Temples that stayed: 1921 shrines and temples
legend.mapchallenge.day06.templeYes: A registered temple within 100 m today
legend.mapchallenge.day06.templeSame: Same name today: a temple of the same name nearby ({n})
legend.mapchallenge.day06.templeNote: 1,007 of 1,439 (70%) still have a registered temple within 100 m; shifting every point 300 or 600 m gives only about 9%. Unregistered small shrines are missing from today's list, so this is a lower bound. The {n} named sites with a same-name temple today are ringed and labelled from z13.
legend.mapchallenge.day06.lighthouseTitl: Lighthouses and weather stations, then and now
legend.mapchallenge.day06.lighthouseNote: All five weather stations set up in 1896–97 are still staffed CWA stations; Taipei is only 10 m away. Today's list has only 36 main lighthouses, so 'no match' does not mean gone; the Pengjia Islet point lies at sea and is treated as a digitising error.
legend.mapchallenge.day06.sourceShort: Academia Sinica, Taiwan History and Culture in Atlas, 1st ed. (2003), CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 Taiwan; derived data under the same terms (non-commercial)
